title: Kestrel GAP Waiver Benefit Determination
content:
# Kestrel GAP Waiver Benefit Determination

## 1. Waiver status

A claim is decided only on a waiver whose status is active. The same holds for paying the benefit. The status is taken from the company's waiver record for the waiver the claim is on.

## 2. Denials

A claim is denied with the following decisions:

- **denied — no primary insurance**, when no physical damage insurance was in force at the loss;
- **denied — loss before waiver**, when the loss date is before the waiver sale date;
- **denied — late filing**, when the claim was filed after the claim notice days.

A denied decision records a benefit of 0.00.

## 3. The benefit

Otherwise the claim is approved, and the benefit is defined as follows:

1. **Net shortfall.** The payoff at the loss date, less the insurer settlement, less the benefit exclusions, less rolled-in negative equity where the waiver does not cover it, less financed back-end products where the waiver does not cover them, and less deferred installments beyond the covered number. Where this figure is below zero it is taken as zero.
2. **Covered share.** The waiver's maximum loan-to-value covered, as a percent, applied to the vehicle cash price, then divided by the amount financed at sale; where that quotient is greater than one, the covered share is one. Both the vehicle cash price and the amount financed at sale are the figures recorded on the waiver at its sale.
3. **Covered shortfall.** The net shortfall multiplied by the covered share.
4. **Deductible coverage.** The covered shortfall plus the waiver's deductible coverage, up to the recognized primary deductible.
5. **Ceiling and rounding.** The benefit is the lesser of that total and the waiver's maximum benefit, rounded to the cent. Rounding is applied once, to this final figure.

The benefit is paid to the lienholder within the benefit payment business days. Paying the benefit settles the waiver: its status becomes claim settled.

## 4. Reconsideration

A denied claim can be reconsidered when new documents arrive within the reconsideration days.

## Figures by level

| Level | Maximum loan-to-value covered | Deductible coverage (USD) | Maximum benefit (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kestrel GAP Essential | 115 percent | 0.00 | 25000.00 |
| Kestrel GAP Standard | 125 percent | 0.00 | 35000.00 |
| Kestrel GAP Plus | 125 percent | 500.00 | 50000.00 |
| Kestrel GAP Premier | 150 percent | 500.00 | 50000.00 |
| Kestrel GAP Premier Plus | 150 percent | 1000.00 | 75000.00 |
| Kestrel GAP Max | 175 percent | 1000.00 | 100000.00 |

## Worked example (hypothetical claim)

A Kestrel GAP Plus waiver sold on a contract with a vehicle cash price of 20000.00 and an amount financed at sale of 27000.00. Insurance was in force, the loss is after the sale date and the claim was filed in time. Payoff at the loss date 24000.00; insurer settlement 15000.00; no exclusions or uncovered items; primary deductible 1000.00.

| Line | Figure |
|---|---|
| Net shortfall: 24000.00 less 15000.00 | 9000.00 |
| Covered share: 125 percent of 20000.00 is 25000.00, divided by 27000.00 | 0.925925… (less than one, so kept) |
| Covered shortfall: 9000.00 multiplied by the covered share | 8333.333… |
| Plus deductible coverage of 500.00, within the recognized deductible of 1000.00 | 8833.333… |
| Lesser of that total and the 50000.00 maximum benefit, rounded to the cent | **8833.33** |

Had the amount financed at sale been 22000.00, 25000.00 divided by 22000.00 exceeds one, so the covered share would be one and the benefit 9500.00.
